sections.heading: A short route through Dylan's history
paragraphs: Start with the Ordinary AWE: Jesse and Dylan encountered an Altered World Event as children, and the Bureau's response separated their lives. Dylan was taken into FBC custody and labelled P6 under the Prime Candidate program. In CONTROL, Jesse entered the Oldest House looking for him. Resonant reverses the direction of that search: Dylan goes out into Manhattan looking for Jesse.

This sequence explains why three names recur in files about Dylan: Ordinary is the incident, P6 is the Bureau designation, and the Oldest House is where his confinement took place. None of those is a Resonant upgrade category. Zoe's role as field handler belongs to the present crisis, while Jesse and the Bureau explain the history Dylan carries into it.

sections.heading: Jesse's story versus Dylan's objective
paragraphs: Jesse's search through the Oldest House is the spine of CONTROL (2019). That game establishes her as Director and reunites the Faden siblings after years of separation. A wiki page about Jesse therefore contains two different kinds of information: established history from the first game and the still-unanswered question of where she is during Resonant.

For the sequel, the useful chain is Ordinary to the Prime Candidate files, then the Oldest House, then Dylan's search in Manhattan. Do not mistake an older Jesse ability guide or Bureau collectible for a confirmed Resonant objective. The announced playable lead is Dylan; Jesse's absence supplies a story motive, not a second announced character campaign.

sections.heading: How Zoe connects the field operation
paragraphs: Zoe belongs to the present-day side of this story. Dylan knows the Bureau through confinement inside the Oldest House; Zoe has lived through the Manhattan emergency outside it. Her handler role puts those perspectives in direct contact as the player moves through distinct city zones.

This makes her a useful orientation point rather than an assumed quest dispenser. When dialogue describes a new location, separate the immediate field objective from the Bureau's wider interpretation of the crisis. The published material establishes a working relationship and exploration dialogue, but not a complete list of Zoe missions, choices or rewards.

sections.heading: A weapon, a loadout, and a resource loop
paragraphs: The Aberrant is one transforming weapon, not a collection of six unrelated drops. A build combines a Primary Form, a Secondary Form and a Combo Ender. The Forms page compares the named early choices by combat role; this page explains the system holding them together. The Gap is where players review and change the resulting setup outside combat.

The reason to compare Forms is the resource loop around them. Melee hits restore Combat Ability resource, abilities can stun enemies, and executions temporarily improve melee damage. A slower or wider attack pattern changes how easily you keep that loop going against a given group. Preview footage shows the principle, not reliable final damage rankings for each Form.

sections.heading: Movement unlock, not attack selection
paragraphs: Reach is associated with traversal through the previewed Metro Fault. It belongs in a different mental category from Barrage, Seekers and Shield, the Combat Ability choices described after an early Resonant encounter. That difference matters when reading preview routes: gaining Reach opens a way across space rather than occupying one of the attack choices shown in a combat menu.

The published route gives a useful example of a world ability that can gate movement. It does not establish every place Reach will be required, a complete unlock order, or a final collectible path. New Game Plus information says story-gated traversal abilities are reacquired, so a returning build may be strong while its movement route still depends on story progress.

sections.heading: How the city is organized for players
paragraphs: Resonant's Manhattan is described as a set of distinct, handcrafted zones, not an endlessly repeating open-world checklist. The FBC Field Office connects those areas as a hub. Within a zone, the published structure separates Dylan's Journey, self-contained World Quests, combat encounters, environmental challenges and discoveries.

That hierarchy is more useful than treating every preview image as a named map marker. Start with a zone and the activity type you are pursuing; then use the relevant mission or world file for context. No official full map, exact collectible coordinates or final count of activities has been released for this pre-launch index.

sections.heading: Which game does this location belong to?
paragraphs: The Oldest House was the central playable setting of CONTROL. It housed the Bureau, its containment work, Jesse's search for Dylan and the P6 records that explain his confinement. That history is relevant to Resonant, but a room-by-room guide to the 2019 building is not automatically a guide to the new game's Manhattan zones.

For a new player, the important connection is institutional: the same FBC that studied Dylan inside the House deploys him outside during a citywide crisis. For a returning player, it helps explain why familiar names such as Darling, Pope and Arish carry different meanings for Dylan than they did for Jesse.

sections.heading: Using a preview zone without inventing a map
paragraphs: The West Incursion Zone is useful because it is a concrete example of the city's altered architecture and combat spaces. It shows what a named Manhattan area can look like, but it should not be read as a complete region guide. Preview cuts can rearrange encounters and leave out paths, transitions or objective text.

When looking for a route, first ask whether the activity is part of Dylan's Journey, a World Quest, or an environmental challenge. Then look for a published mission preview such as Metro Fault rather than deriving directions from a cinematic montage. This entry deliberately contains no unverified collectible pins or completion checklist.

sections.heading: What the preview route actually establishes
paragraphs: Metro Fault is one named underground preview route, with transit hazards, Mold opposition and the Reach movement reward. Those elements make it a useful example of how traversal and combat can meet in a Fault. They are not evidence for a universal Fault template, a guaranteed reward table or a complete launch walkthrough.

The key reading distinction is between observed sequence and inferred route. The footage establishes the encounter ingredients and Reach association; it does not supply every turn, checkpoint or optional pickup. For a practical run, treat Reach as the significant unlock and return to a step-by-step guide only when its route can be checked against the shipped game.

paragraphs: The Central Resonant preview distinguishes this fight through lava-like floor danger and magma attacks. A Resonant encounter also matters to progression because an early hands-on describes a post-fight Combat Ability choice. Do not assume every Resonant battle has identical rewards or that the unnamed first entity is the same enemy as the Central Resonant. The two preview files are kept separate for that reason.

sections.heading: A practical order for checking a new build
paragraphs: The Gap joins several systems that are easy to confuse. Start by checking the Aberrant's Primary and Secondary Forms, then the Combat Ability choice, then Talents and crafted Artifacts. An Untapped Artifact found in the world is a crafting input; it is not already an equipped passive. The Gap is also described as a place to test a build before taking it into another encounter.

This order is a planning aid, not a prescribed optimal build. The published material shows different roles for Forms and abilities but no trustworthy final ranking. NG+ expands combinations and carries much combat progress forward, while story-gated movement still has to be reacquired.

sections.heading: The hub's place in the route
paragraphs: The Field Office is the central Manhattan hub linking handcrafted zones. That tells players something about the game's geography: traveling between named areas is not the same as walking across one continuous open-world street grid. It also distinguishes the present field operation from the FBC's older headquarters inside the Oldest House.

A hub can organize a route without proving which services, NPCs or quest boards it contains at launch. Zoe is confirmed as Dylan's field handler, but her exact office location and a complete hub feature list should not be inferred from the role. Use the hub as the relationship between zones, not as a fabricated map with marked collectibles.

sections.heading: What the Form comparison can and cannot tell you
paragraphs: A Form's useful first distinction is role: fast pressure, reach, broad coverage or a heavier commitment. The published early pool identifies Primary and Secondary choices, while Combo Enders provide another part of the weapon setup. Selecting a pair is therefore more informative than asking for a single best Form in isolation.

Official previews explain that close-range hits replenish Combat Ability resource. That means a Form's attack pattern affects how a player maintains the melee–ability–execution loop. The available footage does not justify a final numerical tier list, exact upgrade cost or universal boss recommendation. Treat the comparison table as a starting role map and test combinations in the Gap.

sections.heading: Choosing for a situation rather than a tier list
paragraphs: The early Barrage, Seekers and Shield choice presents different functions, not a published best-to-worst ranking. The useful question is what your current weapon pair lacks: ranged pressure, autonomous targeting or protection while closing distance. An ability can also stun an enemy and create an execution opening, which feeds back into melee damage.

The choice described in a hands-on follows a Resonant encounter, but it should not be generalized into a guaranteed reward for every boss. NG+ later broadens ability combinations; a first-run choice and a second-run loadout are not the same decision. The Gap is where the available options are managed.

sections.heading: From discovery to an equipped effect
paragraphs: The important sequence is discovery, crafting and equipping. Untapped Artifacts are found during exploration, then crafted into usable Artifacts in the Gap. An Artifact changes a build as a passive component, alongside the active decisions made through the Aberrant and Combat Abilities. That is why a list of discovered names cannot be treated as an inventory of currently equipped effects.

The announced first-run limit is three Artifact slots, with a fourth opening in New Game Plus. That is a capacity rule, not proof of every Artifact's final effect, rarity or crafting ingredient. Compare an Artifact by what it adds to your present combat loop rather than assuming every found object belongs in a strongest-build list.

sections.heading: What a second run changes in practice
paragraphs: NG+ retains Aberrant upgrades, health and combat-resource improvements, unlocked supernatural Combat Abilities, Talents and Artifacts. It also permits broader combinations, including the additional Artifact slot. The player therefore begins with combat options that were earned across the first run instead of repeating the same opening build decisions from zero.

That carryover is not universal. Story-gated traversal tools are reacquired as the route unfolds, so an upgraded weapon does not imply immediate access to every area. Read progression as two tracks: the build you bring forward and the route you still need to reopen. This distinction is especially relevant to previewed movement abilities such as Reach.

sections.heading: A route-planning vocabulary
paragraphs: Dylan's Journey names the main campaign; World Quests are self-contained narrative stories. Faults are another activity type, with Metro Fault providing a concrete published example. This vocabulary helps a player decide whether to follow the central plot, pursue a side story or inspect a contained challenge, without pretending a complete quest log has been published.

The city also contains combat encounters, environmental challenges and discoveries. These do not all become separate missions simply because they appear in a preview. If you are searching for a named route, start with the Metro Fault file. If you are choosing how to spend time in a zone, start with the Manhattan overview.

The Prime Candidate file explains the designation; the Ordinary file explains why the Bureau became interested in the siblings in the first place.

That chain is useful when the sequel invokes old Bureau language. It does not establish Darling's location, allegiance or services in Manhattan. Distinguish an archival account of what he did to Dylan from a new scene that would show what he does now.

sections.heading: A relationship map for the sequel
paragraphs: The Bureau is not a single character with one view of Dylan. The P6 program and Darling's research belong to the history of his confinement. Jesse became Director in CONTROL. Zoe is the field agent who works with him during Resonant's Manhattan emergency. Those roles make the agency both a source of harm in his past and an operational partner in the present.

Reading FBC pages in that order prevents an easy continuity mistake: the Oldest House was the central setting of the original game, while the Field Office connects the new game's city zones. A familiar logo or title alone does not tell you which period a file is describing.

sections.heading: Why Ordinary is the start of this family story
paragraphs: The Ordinary AWE is a past event from CONTROL's history, not a newly announced Resonant mission. Jesse and Dylan encountered the Slide Projector as children, after which the Bureau took a close interest in both. Their paths diverged: Dylan was brought into custody and marked P6, while Jesse later came to the Oldest House searching for him.

That event gives meaning to the sequel's reversal. Dylan is no longer the missing child Jesse sought inside the Bureau's headquarters; he is the playable lead looking for her outside in Manhattan. The event also explains why P6 and P7 appear in old files, but neither label is a class or skill tree in Resonant.

sections.heading: Reading P6 and P7 correctly
paragraphs: P6 and P7 are Bureau labels for Dylan and Jesse within the Prime Candidate program. They belong to the organization's search for a future Director after the Ordinary incident. The labels are valuable when reading old files because they identify which sibling a report concerns even when a personal name is absent.

They are not player ranks, playable character slots or sequel character classes. Dylan's Resonant build is defined through the Aberrant, Combat Abilities, Talents and Artifacts instead. Darling's connection is that he supervised research into Dylan; Jesse's later Director role belongs to the outcome of the first game, not a promised path for the player to select in Resonant.

paragraphs: If distance is the problem, compare Extend's extra reach with a Combat Ability such as Barrage before changing the whole build. If a crowd keeps interrupting a narrow attack, Slash's wide arc is the more relevant Form to inspect. These are differences in the shown roles, not a promise that either option wins every fight.

A Form also changes how you return to melee after spending a power. The Aberrant file explains that shared resource loop; the Gap file explains where the parts of a loadout are reviewed. Keep weapon role, ability choice and build management separate when comparing them.

sections.heading: Choose a role, then check its cost
paragraphs: Barrage answers distance with a projectile, Seekers add pressure that is not tied to Dylan's next weapon swing, and Shield covers a defensive opening before a forward attack. The early preview presents these as a choice, so reading them as three simultaneous starting powers would give a false picture of the first run.

All three sit inside the same melee-fed resource loop. If a chosen power feels scarce, the next question is whether the equipped Aberrant Forms allow a safe return to weapon hits—not whether the power has an unpublished cooldown or hidden upgrade.

sections.heading: An old threat in a new setting
paragraphs: The Hiss defined the emergency inside the Oldest House in CONTROL. Resonant material names it among the threats affecting Manhattan, but the exact roster and behavior of its new-game enemy variants cannot be copied from the 2019 bestiary. The city introduces a different setting, movement system and melee-focused combat loop.

When a preview shows an enemy, distinguish its visible attack from its presumed faction. Metro Fault also features Mold opposition; Resonants form another encounter category. Grouping all three under 'Hiss' would make an enemy index easier to fill but less useful in play. This file preserves the continuity context while leaving new-game combat claims to observed encounters.
